summary: # How to Start 3D Design from Scratch: Pattern Making and Creating a Pair of Pants in CLO ## Introduction Hello everyone, this is the second episode of the video tutorial on how to adjust the model of the pants for the top. Please refer to the opening content of the top in CLO. ## Creating the Width First of all, create a width. Extend the width. The difference between the width of the waist and the width of the high knees is 500mm x 1030mm. Lower the hump by 15mm and provide head space. Mark with the lines and mark at the base depth of 250mm. Additionally, mark with the lines and mark at the base depth of 350mm. ## Pocket Adjustments Reduce the length of the pocket to 40mm and use the inner line to mark 81mm from the bottom to the end of the line. Use the plus point division tool; there is a button on the line. Select the first option, divide it into two lines, and enter the corresponding color size. Mark the width of the front pocket piece to 245mm. ## Front Pocket Piece Width Use the plus point division tool to mark the width of the front pocket piece to 60mm. Add the width of the front pocket piece and the maximum width. At first, press the button on the corner. Press the plus pin, select the bottom piece, and select the edge part to mark the width. There are several ways to mark the width; the width of the front pocket piece should be around 90 to 95mm. ## Vertical Position Adjustments Increase the list end point to the homologator and use the plus point division tool to mark the width, where the width and height is 95mm. Extend the vertical position of this point up to 60mm, ensuring the mouth is parallel to this point, so that the mouth needs to be folded. The same line should connect to the mouth of the foot, and the front blade should connect to the mouth of the foot. ## Front Blade Design To design the needs, we will tilt the front blade 6mm at the waistline and tilt it 5mm outwards. Connect the two points. Press and hold the end point while pressing and holding the control button simultaneously to create an extension point on the line. ## Reference Line Adjustments Find the two focal points and divide the distance between the front blade width and the inner seam. Mark the center point and the line. We will turn the reference line into the baseline to make the picture cleaner. Let’s draw the line and turn the reference line up and down. ## Drawing and Adjustments To join the lines, place the kuribayi in the center line and draw the one point. Please like and subscribe to my channel. Until the next video. ## Using the Multidirectional Line Tool Use the built-in multidirectional line tool to draw a front wave. Press the control key to draw a curve, and then press the keypad to show the point of the curve, which can be adjusted. Begin by making a 60mm long vertical line, then select the point of the curve and press the CTRL key to move based on the extension line. ## Knee Position Marking Use the plus sign tool to mark the position of the knee towards the inside by 10mm. Press the control key to draw a curve repeatedly for adjustments. To draw the inner gap of the outer edge, we can use the edit tool to quickly cut the line. ## Curve Adjustments Use the Editor-in-Chief tool to adjust the speed of the shortcut C to a large range, and then switch to the Editor-in-Chief curve point tool to adjust the details of the V-shape. Press the Shift key to select the V-shape and then press the Right key to select the V-shape. Clean up the V-shape by deleting all unnecessary points and lines. ## Completing the Front Piece After sewing the center of the leg, use the edit tool to increase the rope, insert the rope and the rope. Click OK. After clicking OK, you can adjust the outer frame line after sewing the rope to modify the curve situation. Complete the post-processing and make a good rope. Use the edit tool to select the inner line, double-click to cross the cross point, and right-click to convert to the baseline. ## Creating the Back Piece The back piece is based on the front piece as the base to make the board. Copy the draft of the front piece first. Use the edit tool on the left-hand side of the board. Right-click on the board to expand the outline of the board by 100mm. ## Setting Reference Lines Now, place the piece of the bag in the darter for the table. If there is a reference value but the line is not used, it can be converted into a basic line first. The center line is set to 20mm and converted into a baseline. ## Extending the Base Line At the 45mm mark on the top of the bottom line, connect this point to the last point to make a vertical line. Extend this baseline to 265mm to make the back of the leg wider. After the joint point, select the joint line and press the CTRL key to create a vertical line as the basic movement to the hip position. ## Final Adjustments Measure the distance from the outside seam to the center of the back of the leg and make a position on the right side of this distance. Remove it and create an internal line of 20mm from the front. Set a vertical line to 25mm to line up both sides. ## Waist and Belt Adjustments Connect points to draw the initial line and extend the outer side of the seam to shape the edge. Measure the center of the waist to the knee, reducing this distance to 0 to 10mm, and position it on the back wave. Draw the waistline reference line at the connection point. ## Curve and Seam Adjustments Change the reference line to the baseline to make the picture cleaner. After dividing the inner points, extend the back wave reference line to the focal point and convert it to a baseline. Adjust the back wave reference line to be 5mm thinner. ## Completing the Design From this point to the left, set the waist width of 4cm to 1cm, plus the weight of 40mm, which is 225mm. Draw a reference line on this point and convert it to the back wave reference line. Then change the back wave reference line back to the baseline. ## Final Touches Copy the outer side of the front as reference lines, then paste it. Place the end of the line at the knee position. Change to the book edition tool and turn the center point, dragging it to the knee point. ## Finalizing the Pants The vertical extension line of the vertical position of the right waistline can be aligned smoothly. First, convert the straight line point into a curve point. Then convert the reference line into the baseline before aligning the curve line smoothly. ## Panel Arrangement Use the internal multidirectional line tool C to draw the waistline. The length of the back side of the seam should be 5mm shorter than the front side. Adjust the width of the curve line to 6mm and texture the curve point. Use the internal multidirectional line tool G to draw a back wave and adjust the shape. ## Simulation and Adjustments Turn the reference line of the inner seam into the baseline, draw the inner seam, and create a curve line using the control key. Use the tool to frame the outline, select the outline with the Shift key, and frame it as a panel. ## Conclusion Thank you for watching.
